claim: Crystal structures of ectodomain fragments comprising cell-cell recognition regions of mouse γ-Pcdhs γA1, γA8, γB2, and γB7 reveal trans-homodimers.
source: Here we report crystal structures of ectodomain fragments comprising cell-cell recognition regions of mouse γ-Pcdhs γA1, γA8, γB2, and γB7 revealing trans-homodimers
evidence: The abstract directly states that crystal structures were determined and that they reveal trans-homodimers.

claim: Crystal structures of C-terminal ectodomain fragments from γ-Pcdhs γA4 and γB2 depict cis-interacting regions in monomeric form.
source: Here we report crystal structures of ectodomain fragments comprising cell-cell recognition regions of mouse γ-Pcdhs γA1, γA8, γB2, and γB7 revealing trans-homodimers, and of C-terminal ectodomain fragments from γ-Pcdhs γA4 and γB2, which depict cis-interacting regions in monomeric form.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that structures of C-terminal fragments were determined and are in monomeric form.

claim: The reported structures span the entire γ-Pcdh ectodomain.
source: Together these structures span the entire γ-Pcdh ectodomain.
evidence: The abstract states that the collection of structures covers the entire ectodomain.

claim: The trans-dimer structures reveal determinants of γ-Pcdh isoform-specific homophilic recognition.
source: The trans-dimer structures reveal determinants of γ-Pcdh isoform-specific homophilic recognition.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that the structures reveal specificity determinants.

claim: Cis-dimerization mutations were identified and structurally mapped to the C-terminal ectodomain structures.
source: We identified and structurally mapped cis-dimerization mutations to the C-terminal ectodomain structures.
evidence: The abstract states that mutations were identified and mapped to structures.

claim: Pcdh ectodomains from γB-subfamily isoforms formed cis dimers.
source: Biophysical studies showed that Pcdh ectodomains from γB-subfamily isoforms formed cis dimers
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that biophysical studies demonstrated cis dimer formation for γB isoforms.

claim: Pcdh ectodomains from γA isoforms did not form cis dimers.
source: Biophysical studies showed that Pcdh ectodomains from γB-subfamily isoforms formed cis dimers, whereas γA isoforms did not
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that γA isoforms did not form cis dimers in biophysical studies.

claim: Both γA and γB isoforms can interact in cis with α-Pcdhs.
source: Biophysical studies showed that Pcdh ectodomains from γB-subfamily isoforms formed cis dimers, whereas γA isoforms did not, but both γA and γB isoforms could interact in cis with α-Pcdhs.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that both γA and γB can interact with α-Pcdhs in cis.

claim: Interaction specificity is distributed over all domains of the γ-Pcdh trans interface.
source: Together, these data show how interaction specificity is distributed over all domains of the γ-Pcdh trans interface
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this conclusion based on the data presented.

claim: Subfamily- or isoform-specific cis-interactions may play a role in the Pcdh-mediated neuronal self-recognition code.
source: Together, these data show how interaction specificity is distributed over all domains of the γ-Pcdh trans interface, and suggest that subfamily- or isoform-specific cis-interactions may play a role in the Pcdh-mediated neuronal self-recognition code.
evidence: The abstract suggests this as a conclusion based on the observed differences in cis interactions.

claim: Dendrites and axonal arbors of the same neuron do not stably contact one another in neural circuit assembly.
source: A characteristic of neural circuit assembly is that dendrites and axonal arbors of the same neuron do not stably contact one another, but are free to interact with the processes of other neurons (Zipursky and Grueber, 2013; Zipursky and Sanes, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of neural circuit assembly and supported by citations.

claim: Self-avoidance is accomplished through a mechanism that mediates self-avoidance between sister branches from individual neurons while permitting interactions between non-self neurons.
source: This fundamental property of neural circuit assembly is accomplished through a mechanism that mediates 'self-avoidance' between sister branches from individual neurons, while permitting interactions between non-self neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a fundamental property of neural circuit assembly.

claim: Self-avoidance requires the generation of unique single cell surface identities through stochastic expression of unique combinations of cell surface protein isoforms in both vertebrates and invertebrates.
source: In both vertebrates and invertebrates, self-avoidance is thought to require the generation of unique single cell surface identities through mechanisms that involve the stochastic expression of unique combinations of cell surface protein isoforms (Zipursky and Grueber, 2013; Chen and Maniatis, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a thought/hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: In Drosophila and many other invertebrates, individual-neuron identities are provided by the expression of single-cell-specific Dscam1-isoform subsets generated by stochastic alternative splicing.
source: In Drosophila and many other invertebrates individual-neuron identities are provided by the expression of single-cell-specific Dscam1-isoform subsets generated by stochastic alternative splicing (Miura et al., 2013; Schmucker et al., 2000; Wojtowicz et al., 2004; Neves et al., 2004; Zhan et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as a mechanism in invertebrates and supported by multiple citations.

claim: In vertebrates, clustered protocadherins (Pcdhs) provide cell-surface diversity through stochastic alternative promoter choice.
source: By contrast, in vertebrates the clustered protocadherins (Pcdhs) provide analogous cell-surface diversity, but in this case generated through stochastic alternative promoter choice (Tasic et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2002; Esumi et al., 2005; Hirano et al., 2012; Kaneko et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as the vertebrate mechanism and supported by citations.

claim: Both invertebrate Dscam1 proteins and vertebrate Pcdhs are highly diverse families of cell-surface proteins that form isoform-specific trans-dimers between apposed neuronal cell surfaces.
source: Both the invertebrate Dscam1 proteins, and vertebrate Pcdhs are highly diverse families of cell-surface proteins that form isoform-specific trans-dimers between apposed neuronal cell surfaces (Zipursky and Grueber, 2013; Zipursky and Sanes, 2010; Chen and Maniatis, 2013; Thu et al., 2014; Schreiner and Weiner, 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a property of both protein families and supported by citations.

claim: Stochastic alternative splicing of the Dscam1 gene in D. melanogaster produces up to 19,008 distinct protein isoforms.
source: Stochastic alternative splicing of the Dscam1 gene in D. melanogaster produces up to 19,008 distinct protein isoforms, the majority of which engage in highly specific trans homodimerization (Miura et al., 2013; Schmucker et al., 2000; Wojtowicz et al., 2004, 2007).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about Dscam1 diversity and supported by citations.

claim: The majority of Dscam1 isoforms engage in highly specific trans homodimerization.
source: Stochastic alternative splicing of the Dscam1 gene in D. melanogaster produces up to 19,008 distinct protein isoforms, the majority of which engage in highly specific trans homodimerization (Miura et al., 2013; Schmucker et al., 2000; Wojtowicz et al., 2004, 2007).
evidence: This is stated as a property of Dscam1 isoforms and supported by citations.

claim: Mice and humans express 58 and 53 distinct Pcdh isoforms, respectively.
source: In contrast, mice and humans express just 58 and 53 distinct Pcdh isoforms, respectively, each of which display isoform-specific homophilic binding in trans (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about Pcdh diversity in mice and humans.

claim: Each Pcdh isoform displays isoform-specific homophilic binding in trans.
source: In contrast, mice and humans express just 58 and 53 distinct Pcdh isoforms, respectively, each of which display isoform-specific homophilic binding in trans (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a property of Pcdh isoforms and supported by citations.

claim: Biophysical measurements with domain-deleted proteins showed that Pcdhs interact in cis through a membrane-proximal dimer interface involving extracellular cadherin domain 6 (EC6) and potentially EC5.
source: Biophysical measurements with domain-deleted proteins showed that Pcdhs also interact in cis, through a membrane-proximal dimer interface involving extracellular cadherin domain 6 (EC6) and potentially EC5 (Thu et al., 2014; Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from biophysical measurements and supported by citations.

claim: Pcdh cis dimers are thought to form promiscuously.
source: Pcdh cis dimers are thought to form promiscuously (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014), and thus provide a large repertoire of cis dimeric Pcdh recognition units (Rubinstein et al., 2015; Thu et al., 2014).

claim: Promiscuous cis dimer formation provides a large repertoire of cis dimeric Pcdh recognition units.
source: Pcdh cis dimers are thought to form promiscuously (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Thu et al., 2014), and thus provide a large repertoire of cis dimeric Pcdh recognition units (Rubinstein et al., 2015; Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of promiscuous cis dimer formation and supported by citations.

claim: Vertebrate protocadherin genes have a unique organization in which the Pcdhα, Pcdhβ, and Pcdhγ gene clusters are arranged in tandem.
source: Vertebrate protocadherin genes have a unique organization in which the Pcdhα, Pcdhβ, and Pcdhγ gene clusters are arranged in tandem (Wu and Maniatis, 1999).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about Pcdh gene organization and supported by a citation.

claim: Each Pcdh gene cluster contains multiple alternative variable exons (14 Pcdhα, 22 Pcdhβ, and 22 Pcdhγ in the mouse).
source: Each of the Pcdh gene clusters contains multiple alternative variable exons (14 Pcdhα, 22 Pcdhβ, and 22 Pcdhγ in the mouse) which encode full Pcdh ectodomains, including six extracellular cadherin (EC) domains, a single transmembrane region and a short cytoplasmic extension.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the gene cluster organization.

claim: Variable exons encode full Pcdh ectodomains, including six extracellular cadherin (EC) domains, a single transmembrane region and a short cytoplasmic extension.
source: Each of the Pcdh gene clusters contains multiple alternative variable exons (14 Pcdhα, 22 Pcdhβ, and 22 Pcdhγ in the mouse) which encode full Pcdh ectodomains, including six extracellular cadherin (EC) domains, a single transmembrane region and a short cytoplasmic extension.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about what the variable exons encode.

claim: The Pcdhα and Pcdhγ gene clusters contain three 'constant' exons that encode cluster-specific intracellular domains.
source: The Pcdhα and Pcdhγ gene clusters also contain three 'constant' exons that encode cluster-specific intracellular domains.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the gene cluster organization.

claim: The last two variable exons in the Pcdhα gene cluster and the last three variable exons of the Pcdhγ gene cluster are divergent from other Pcdh 'alternate' isoforms and are referred to as 'C-type' Pcdhs.
source: The last two variable exons in the Pcdhα gene cluster and the last three variable exons of the Pcdhγ gene cluster are divergent from other Pcdh 'alternate' isoforms and are referred to as 'C-type' Pcdhs (Wu and Maniatis, 1999; Wu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about C-type Pcdhs and supported by citations.

claim: Non-C-type Pcdhγ genes have been divided into two subfamilies—PcdhγA and PcdhγB—based on sequence identity/phylogenetic analysis.
source: The non-C-type Pcdhγ genes have been further divided into two subfamilies—PcdhγA and PcdhγB—based on sequence identity/phylogenetic analysis (Wu and Maniatis, 1999).
evidence: This is stated as a classification based on sequence analysis and supported by a citation.

claim: Single-cell RT-PCR studies of the Pcdhα and Pcdhγ clusters in Purkinje neurons revealed that each neuron expresses all C-type Pcdhs biallelically, along with ~10 alternate isoforms stochastically expressed from each gene cluster independently on allelic chromosomes.
source: Single-cell RT-PCR studies of the Pcdhα and Pcdhγ clusters in Purkinje neurons revealed that each neuron expresses all C-type Pcdhs biallelically, along with ~10 alternate isoforms (α, β, and γ) stochastically expressed from each gene cluster independently on allelic chromosomes (Esumi et al., 2005; Kaneko et al., 2006).

claim: Knockouts of the Pcdhα gene cluster revealed neuronal wiring defects in olfactory and serotonergic neurons.
source: Knockouts of the Pcdhα gene cluster revealed neuronal wiring defects in olfactory and serotonergic neurons (Hasegawa et al., 2008, 2012; Katori et al., 2009).

claim: Genetic ablation of the Pcdhγ gene cluster leads to lethality at P0.
source: By contrast, genetic ablation of the Pcdhγ gene cluster leads to lethality at P0 (Lefebvre et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2002), and revealed a cell-death phenotype for some neuron types (Wang et al., 2002; Weiner et al., 2005; Lefebvre et al., 2008; Prasad and Weiner, 2011; Chen et al., 2012).

claim: Genetic ablation of the Pcdhγ gene cluster revealed a cell-death phenotype for some neuron types.

claim: γ-Pcdhs act locally to regulate dendrite arborization, with the complexity of a neuron's dendritic arbor determined, at least in part, by Pcdh-dependent non-cell autonomous interaction of a neuron with surrounding neurons and glia.
source: Subsequent studies with transgenic and conditional knockout mice suggest that γ-Pcdhs act locally to regulate dendrite arborization, with the complexity of a neuron's dendritic arbor determined, at least in part, by Pcdh-dependent non-cell autonomous interaction of a neuron with surrounding neurons and glia (Molumby et al., 2016).

claim: Formation of self-synapses (autapses) is observed in starburst amacrine cells upon deletion of the Pcdhγ cluster.
source: Deletion of all 22 genes in the Pcdhγ cluster in mice results in a loss of dendritic self-avoidance in retinal starburst amacrine cells and cerebellar Purkinje cells (Lefebvre et al., 2012), with formation of self-synapses (autapses) observed in starburst amacrine cells (Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015).

claim: Most neuron types appeared unaffected by the loss of the Pcdhγ gene cluster.

claim: Recognition between cells expressing multiple Pcdhs is only observed when all expressed isoforms match.

source: The absence of this interaction in some of the γA crystal structures is therefore likely an artifact of crystallization, perhaps due to crystallization condition, although it does imply that the EC1:EC4 interaction is not particularly stable.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the structural findings.

claim: The EC1:EC4 interaction is not particularly stable in γA-Pcdhs.
source: The absence of this interaction in some of the γA crystal structures is therefore likely an artifact of crystallization, perhaps due to crystallization condition, although it does imply that the EC1:EC4 interaction is not particularly stable.
evidence: This is implied by the observation that the EC1:EC4 interaction is absent in some crystal structures.

claim: The EC1–4 dimers of isoforms from the same subfamily have similar overall structures (RMSDs ~1.5–3.4 Å).
source: Excluding the structurally diverse γA-Pcdhs and the partially occluded γB3 dimer (Nicoludis et al., 2016), the EC1–4 dimers of isoforms from the same subfamily have similar overall structures (RMSDs ~1.5–3.4 Å; Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from structural comparison and supported by data.

claim: Superpositions of dimers from different subfamilies revealed larger RMSDs due to distinct relative orientations of the individual protomers (>3.3 Å).
source: In contrast, superpositions of dimers from different subfamilies in general revealed larger RMSDs due to distinct relative orientations of the individual protomers (>3.3 Å; Figure 1—source data 3; Goodman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from structural comparison and supported by data and a citation.

claim: Larger interfamily differences in structure provide an explanation for the absence of α/β, α/γA, β/γA, and β/γB trans dimers.
source: These larger interfamily differences remain apparent when the interaction regions are compared separately, particularly for the EC2–3 dimer regions (Figure 1—source data 4–5). This, in itself, provides a simple explanation for the absence of α/β, α/γA, β/γA, and β/γB trans dimers.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation based on structural differences.

claim: The five trans dimer structures from the α and γB subfamilies exhibited intermediate structural similarity between the two subfamilies (RMSDs ~1.9–3.4 Å).
source: However, the five trans dimer structures from the α and γB subfamilies (excluding the structurally divergent γB3) exhibited intermediate structural similarity between the two subfamilies (RMSDs ~1.9–3.4 Å), which was even more apparent when the EC1:EC4 and EC2–3:EC2–3 interaction regions were compared separately (RMSDs <2.2 Å; Figure 1—source data 4–5).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from structural comparison and supported by data.

claim: The γB7 structure reveals a salt bridge in the EC1:EC4 interface between residues E41 in EC1 and K338 in EC4.
source: The γB7 structure reveals a salt bridge in the EC1:EC4 interface between residues E41 in EC1 and K338 in EC4 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the structure and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Both E41 and K338 are conserved in all γB isoforms so that this salt bridge is likely present in all γB homodimers.
source: Both E41 and K338 are conserved in all γB isoforms so that this salt bridge is likely present in all γB homodimers (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on sequence conservation and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Residue R340, which is conserved in all γB isoforms, is positioned so that it could form an additional salt bridge with E41.
source: In addition, residue R340, which is also conserved in all γB isoforms, is positioned so that it could form an additional salt bridge with E41 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the structure and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: All γA isoforms have an arginine or lysine at position 41.
source: In contrast, all γA isoforms have an arginine or lysine at position 41 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence analysis and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A putative heterodimer formed between any γB isoform and any γA isoform would position a positively charged residue at position 41 in the EC1 domain of the γA isoform in close proximity to K338 and R340 in the γB isoform, which would significantly weaken binding.
source: Thus, a putative heterodimer formed between any γB isoform and any γA isoform would position a positively charged residue at position 41 in the EC1 domain of the γA isoform in close proximity to K338 and R340 in the γB isoform, which would significantly weaken binding (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on structural and sequence analysis and shown in figures.

claim: α-Pcdhs conserve a positive charge at position 40 (structurally equivalent to γB E41).
source: Remarkably, α-Pcdhs also conserve a positive charge at position 40 (structurally equivalent to γB E41), which suggests that putative heterodimers between α-Pcdhs and γB-Pcdhs would also generate electrostatic clashes involving the same residues.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence analysis.

claim: Putative heterodimers between α-Pcdhs and γB-Pcdhs would generate electrostatic clashes involving the same residues.
source: Remarkably, α-Pcdhs also conserve a positive charge at position 40 (structurally equivalent to γB E41), which suggests that putative heterodimers between α-Pcdhs and γB-Pcdhs would also generate electrostatic clashes involving the same residues.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on sequence and structural analysis.

claim: The formation of heterodimers between γB-Pcdhs and both γA-Pcdhs and α-Pcdhs appears to be precluded by the conservation of key charged interface residues in EC1 and EC4.
source: Thus, the formation of heterodimers between γB-Pcdhs and both γA-Pcdhs and α-Pcdhs appears to be precluded by the conservation of key charged interface residues in EC1 and EC4.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the analysis of conserved charged residues.

claim: A similar mechanism has been shown to determine inter-family specificity in the desmosomal cadherins.
source: A similar mechanism has been shown to determine inter-family specificity in the desmosomal cadherins (Harrison et al., 2016) and intra-family specificity in the case of nectins (Harrison et al., 2012; Samanta et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with other protein families and supported by citations.

claim: The majority of isoform-specific trans-interface residues are highly conserved in the same isoform of other species.
source: The logo analysis revealed that the majority of isoform-specific trans-interface residues are highly conserved in the same isoform of other species.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence logo analysis.

claim: EC2:EC3 interacting residues 111 and 294 in the majority of γB2 orthologs are lysine and aspartic acid, which are likely to form a salt bridge in the trans homodimer.
source: For example, EC2:EC3 interacting residues 111 and 294 in the majority of γB2 orthologs (not including mouse) are lysine and aspartic acid, which are likely to form a salt bridge in the trans homodimer
evidence: This is stated as an example of specificity-determining residues based on sequence and structural analysis.

claim: In γB3 and γB7 residue 111 is a conserved glutamic acid, which in the homodimeric complexes interacts favorably with H/R294 in γB3 or S294 in γB7.
source: whilst in γB3 and γB7 residue 111 is a conserved glutamic acid, which in the homodimeric complexes interacts favorably with H/R294 in γB3 or S294 in γB7.
evidence: This is stated as an example of specificity-determining residues based on sequence and structural analysis.

claim: Hypothetical heterodimers between γB2 and γB3 or γB7 would juxtapose like charges E111 (γB3/7):D294 (γB2) and K111 (γB2):H/R294 (γB3) which would disfavor the heterophilic interactions.
source: However hypothetical heterodimers between γB2 and γB3 or γB7 would juxtapose like charges E111 (γB3/7):D294 (γB2) and K111 (γB2):H/R294 (γB3) which would disfavor the heterophilic interactions (Figure 3, γB7 numbering).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion about specificity based on structural and sequence analysis and shown in Figure 3.

claim: All γA EC1–6 molecules tested formed dimers rather than tetramers in solution.
source: All γA EC1–6 molecules we tested formed dimers rather than tetramers in solution (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from AUC experiments and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: γC3EC1–6 was a dimer in solution, although the isodesmic constant was only 1.5 fold larger than the dimer dissociation constant, indicating non-specific binding.
source: γC3EC1–6 was also a dimer in solution, although in this case the isodesmic constant was only 1.5 fold larger than the dimer dissociation constant, indicating non-specific binding.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from AUC experiments.

claim: γA and γC3 EC1–6 dimers are mediated by an EC1–4 (trans) interaction.
source: These EC1–6 dimers are mediated by an EC1–4 (trans) interaction, since all the γA and γC3 EC1–4 fragments we measured were also dimers in solution (Table 1) and the γA and γC3 EC2–6 or EC3–6 fragments were monomers or very weak non-specific dimers (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on AUC data from different fragments and supported by data in tables.

claim: γB2EC1–6, γB4EC1–6, γB5EC1–6, γB6EC1–6, γC5EC1–6, and β5EC1–6 were tetrameric in solution.
source: In contrast, γB2EC1–6, γB4EC1–6, γB5EC1–6, γB6EC1–6, γC5EC1–6, and β5EC1–6 were tetrameric in solution (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from AUC experiments and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: The γB2, γB5, and γB7 EC3–6 fragments were dimers in solution, confirming the presence of the EC6-dependent cis interaction in solution for these γB- and β-Pcdhs.
source: In addition, the γB2, γB5, and γB7 EC3–6 fragments were dimers in solution (Table 2), confirming the presence of the EC6-dependent cis interaction in solution for these γB- and β-Pcdhs, in contrast to the γA-Pcdhs.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from AUC experiments and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: EC6 is highly conserved within non-C-type Pcdh subfamilies.
source: Since EC6 is highly conserved within non-C-type Pcdh subfamilies (Table 3), we assume these results will be general to all mouse β, γA, and γB isoforms.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence analysis and supported by data in Table 3.

claim: The AUC results for EC6-dependent cis interactions will be general to all mouse β, γA, and γB isoforms.
source: Since EC6 is highly conserved within non-C-type Pcdh subfamilies (Table 3), we assume these results will be general to all mouse β, γA, and γB isoforms.
evidence: This is stated as an assumption based on sequence conservation.

claim: β17, γB6, αC2, and γC5 can interact with α-Pcdhs in an EC6-dependent manner.
source: We have previously shown that β17, γB6, αC2, and γC5 can interact with α-Pcdhs in an EC6-dependent manner (Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a previous finding and supported by a citation.

claim: Co-expression of γA3EC5–6 and γA9EC5–6 fragments with Pcdhα4 resulted in cell aggregation.
source: Co-expression of both these isoform fragments with Pcdhα4 resulted in cell aggregation (Figure 5A) indicating that, despite their apparent lack of homophilic cis dimerization, γA-Pcdhs can interact heterophilically with α-Pcdhs in cis.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from cell aggregation assays and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Despite their apparent lack of homophilic cis dimerization, γA-Pcdhs can interact heterophilically with α-Pcdhs in cis.
source: Co-expression of both these isoform fragments with Pcdhα4 resulted in cell aggregation (Figure 5A) indicating that, despite their apparent lack of homophilic cis dimerization, γA-Pcdhs can interact heterophilically with α-Pcdhs in cis.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the cell aggregation assay results.

claim: The γA4EC3–6 and γB2EC3–6 structures are similar overall (RMSD of 3.02 Å over 405 Cα's).
source: The two structures are similar overall (RMSD of 3.02 Å over 405 Cα's), although γA4EC3–6 shows a more pronounced EC4–EC5 bend angle (32.6° for γA4 vs. 18.6° for γB2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from structural comparison.

claim: γA4EC3–6 shows a more pronounced EC4–EC5 bend angle (32.6°) compared to γB2 (18.6°).
source: The two structures are similar overall (RMSD of 3.02 Å over 405 Cα's), although γA4EC3–6 shows a more pronounced EC4–EC5 bend angle (32.6° for γA4 vs. 18.6° for γB2).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from structural analysis.

claim: The γA4 and γB2 EC6 domains have near identical structures (RMSD of 0.80 Å over 90 Cα's).
source: This insertion is the one region of significant structural difference between the γA4 and γB2 EC6 domains, which otherwise have near identical structures (RMSD of 0.80 Å over 90 Cα's).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from structural comparison.

claim: The EC6 domain displays the classic beta sandwich fold, but with a large insertion between the A and A' strands.
source: These are the first Pcdh structures containing EC6, which displays the classic beta sandwich fold, but with a large insertion between the A and A' strands (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated as a description of the EC6 structure and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The G-strands of both EC6 domains are decorated with O-mannose groups on neighboring surface-facing residues, three for γB2 and four for γA4.
source: Notably the G-strands of both EC6 domains are decorated with O-mannose groups on neighboring surface-facing residues, three for γB2 and four for γA4 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the structures and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The EC1–6 trans dimer models predict intermembrane spacings of ~360–375 Å.
source: These models reveal an overall curved shape primarily defined by the EC4–5 bend angle, since both the EC1–4 dimer regions and the EC5–6 tails are relatively straight, and predict intermembrane spacings of ~360–375 Å.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from the structural models.

claim: Three γB6 mutants (L557D, V562D, and R597D) were unable to deliver an α-Pcdh to the cell surface.
source: The majority of the γB6 mutants were able to deliver the α-Pcdh to the cell surface, but three mutants (L557D, V562D, and R597D, γB2 numbering) were not (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from cell aggregation assays and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: All three mutations that disrupted cell surface delivery mapped to the same surface of EC6, specifically to the B and E strands.
source: All three mutations mapped to the same surface of EC6, specifically to the B and E strands (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from mapping mutations to the structure and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The three mutants that were unable to deliver Pcdhα7 to cell surface did not aggregate cells when expressed as full-length PcdhγB6 alone.
source: We also assessed the behavior of these mutants in the full-length γB6 context alone. While most were still able to mediate cell aggregation like wild type γB6 (Thu et al., 2014), the three mutants that were unable to deliver an α-Pcdh to the cell surface in the △EC1 context were also unable to the mediate cell aggregation in the full-length context (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from cell aggregation assays and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The failure of the three mutants to mediate cell aggregation likely results from their failure to reach the cell surface.
source: Since all these mutations are in EC6 they should not affect the EC1–4-mediated trans interaction responsible for cell-cell adhesion in these assays. Thus, the fact that expression of these three mutants does not result in cell aggregation likely results from their failure to reach the cell surface.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the location of the mutations and the assay results.

claim: The γB6EC1–6 V562D mutant was a dimer in solution rather than a tetramer like the wild type.
source: This EC1–6 mutant was a dimer in solution rather than a (cis/trans) tetramer like the wild type (Table 4 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1), indicating the V562D mutation did indeed disrupt homophilic cis interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from AUC experiments and supported by data in Table 4 and a figure.

claim: The V562D mutation disrupted homophilic cis interactions.
source: This EC1–6 mutant was a dimer in solution rather than a (cis/trans) tetramer like the wild type (Table 4 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1), indicating the V562D mutation did indeed disrupt homophilic cis interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the AUC results.

claim: Cell surface delivery of γB isoforms requires EC6-mediated cis interactions.
source: These results also suggest that, like the α-Pcdhs (Thu et al., 2014), cell surface delivery of γB isoforms requires EC6-mediated cis interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the mutagenesis and cell aggregation results and supported by a citation.

claim: All of the 23 residues predicted by PredUs2.0 to be interfacial are located on one side of the EC6 molecule.
source: Remarkably, all of the 23 residues predicted to be interfacial are located on one side of the molecule (Figure 6C and E)—the same side that was identified by mutagenesis.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from computational prediction and shown in figures.

claim: O-mannosylation is observed at EC6 G-strand residues 624, 626, and 628 (γB2 numbering) of both the γB2 and γA4 structures—on the opposite molecular face to the mutations that disrupt cell delivery.
source: Furthermore, O-mannosylation is observed at EC6 G-strand residues 624, 626, and 628 (γB2 numbering) of both the γB2 and γA4 structures—on the opposite molecular face to the mutations that disrupt cell surface delivery (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the structures and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The O-glycan positions at EC6 G-strand residues are usually conserved serines/threonines in α-, β-, and γ-Pcdhs, suggesting that these O-glycans are likely present in all alternate Pcdhs.
source: These positions are usually conserved serines/threonines in α-, β-, and γ-Pcdhs (Figure 6E) suggesting that these O-glycans are likely present in all alternate Pcdhs.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on sequence conservation and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The putative cis interaction region encompasses the A, B, D, and E strands and the BC and DE loops of EC6.
source: Together, these results allowed us to define a putative cis interaction region that encompasses the A, B, D, and E strands and the BC and DE loops of EC6 (Figure 6D–E).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the mutagenesis and computational prediction results and shown in figures.

claim: α-Pcdhs and the carrier β- and γ-Pcdhs differ in nine residues in the putative cis interaction region.
source: Sequence alignment of the EC6 domains for α, β, and γ isoforms shows that α-Pcdhs and the carrier β- and γ-Pcdhs differ in nine residues in this region (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence alignment and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The collection of clustered protocadherin structures now available present a clear picture of how trans-homodimeric interaction specificity is coded for alternate Pcdh isoforms on the trans dimer interface comprising domains EC1–EC4.
source: As discussed below, the collection of clustered protocadherin structures now available present a clear picture of how trans-homodimeric interaction specificity is coded for alternate Pcdh isoforms on the trans dimer interface comprising domains EC1–EC4.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the findings.

claim: γA and γB isoforms are distinct subfamilies with regard to their cis and trans protein interactions.
source: In addition, our data indicate that γA and γB isoforms are distinct subfamilies with regard to their cis and trans protein interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Members of different Pcdh subfamilies fail to bind to each other in trans primarily due to structural differences between the α, β, and γA subfamilies.
source: Our data suggest that members of different subfamilies fail to bind to each other in trans primarily due to structural differences between the α, β, and γA subfamilies.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the structural data.

claim: Members of the γB subfamily are sufficiently similar in structure to members of the α subfamily that a specificity mechanism is unlikely to be based entirely on shape complementarity.
source: However, members of the γB subfamily are sufficiently similar in structure to members of the α subfamily that a specificity mechanism is unlikely to be based entirely on shape complementarity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on structural similarity.

claim: EC1:EC4 interface in γB isoforms will contain salt bridges in the homodimers, whereas the comparable interaction in the inter-subfamily heterodimer would lead to incompatible electrostatic repulsion.
source: Rather, the sequence and structural analyses presented above show that that EC1:EC4 interface in γB isoforms will contain salt bridges in the homodimers, whereas the comparable interaction in the inter-subfamily heterodimer would lead to incompatible electrostatic repulsion.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from sequence and structural analyses.

claim: Electrostatic clashes involving the same residues appear to preclude formation of heterodimers between γB-Pcdhs and γA-Pcdhs.
source: In addition, electrostatic clashes involving the same residues appear to preclude formation of heterodimers between γB-Pcdhs and γA-Pcdhs.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on structural and sequence analyses.

claim: The electrostatic and steric compatibility apparent in homodimer structures would be replaced by incompatibility in putative heterodimers.
source: In agreement with our previous analysis of the α- and β-Pcdhs (Goodman et al., 2016) we find that the electrostatic and steric compatibility apparent in homodimer structures would be replaced by incompatibility in putative heterodimers.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in agreement with previous work and supported by a citation.

claim: Some of the specificity-determining interactions are located in the EC1:EC4 interface and some in the EC2:EC3 interface.
source: As discussed above, some of the specificity-determining interactions are located in the EC1:EC4 interface and some in the EC2:EC3 interface.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the findings.

claim: The findings contradict the conclusion reached by Nicoludis et al. (2016) that EC1:EC4 does not contribute to specificity.
source: These findings, as well as those summarized in the previous paragraph contradict a primary conclusion reached by Nicoludis et al. (2016) that EC1:EC4 does not contribute to specificity.
evidence: This is stated as a contradiction of a previous conclusion and supported by a citation.

claim: Nicoludis et al. used a bioinformatics analysis to infer that trans interaction specificity is mediated by the EC2:EC3 interaction, and that the EC1:EC4 interaction provides affinity, but not specificity.
source: Based on their problematic structure of the EC1–4 trans dimer of PcdhγB3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) and on the four trans-dimeric α and β isoform structures we previously determined (Goodman et al., 2016), Nicoludis et al. used a bioinformatics analysis to infer that trans interaction specificity is mediated by the EC2:EC3 interaction, and that the EC1:EC4 interaction provides affinity, but not specificity.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the conclusions reached by Nicoludis et al. and supported by a citation.

claim: The analysis in this study reveals numerous specificity elements in EC1:EC4 interactions.
source: Our analysis, in contrast, reveals numerous specificity elements in EC1:EC4 interactions.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the analysis in this study.

claim: Cell aggregation experiments with domain-shuffled mutants have clearly demonstrated that specificity is dependent on the identity of EC1 and EC4.
source: Cell aggregation experiments with domain-shuffled mutants have clearly demonstrated that specificity is dependent on the identity of EC1 and EC4 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2; Figure S3 in Rubinstein et al. (2015)).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from cell aggregation experiments and supported by figures and a citation.

claim: For α-Pcdhs, the EC1 and EC4 interface residues are mainly conserved between isoforms.
source: In the case of α-Pcdhs, it is true that the EC1 and EC4 interface residues are mainly conserved between isoforms, as we previously reported (Goodman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work and supported by a citation.

claim: Some α-Pcdh isoforms show conserved differences that determine specificity: α7 shows isoform-specific conservation of trans-interface EC1 residues 36 and 38 and EC4 residues 322 and 324.
source: However, some isoforms show conserved differences that determine specificity: α7 shows isoform-specific conservation of trans-interface EC1 residues 36 and 38 and EC4 residues 322 and 324.
evidence: This is stated as an example of specificity-determining residues.

claim: Swapping EC1:EC4 residues between α7 and α8 swaps their binding preferences.
source: Most importantly, swapping these residues between α7 and α8 swaps their binding preferences (Figure 4—figure supplement 2; Figure 5 in Rubinstein et al. (2015)).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from mutagenesis experiments and supported by figures and a citation.

claim: For β-, γA-, and γB-Pcdhs, isoform-specific conservation of EC1:EC4 trans-interface residues is observed in almost all isoforms.
source: For β-, γA-, and γB-Pcdhs, isoform-specific conservation of EC1:EC4 trans-interface residues is observed in almost all isoforms, as can be seen in sequence logo analysis (Figure 3; Figure 4; and Figure 2 in Goodman et al. (2016)).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence logo analysis and supported by figures and a citation.

claim: Both the EC2:EC3 and EC1:EC4 interfaces play important roles in determining binding specificity.
source: Contrary to the conclusion reached by Nicoludis et al. (2016), these observations, in addition to results from functional mutagenesis experiments showing that changes in specificity result when such residues are mutated (Figure 4—figure supplement 2; Figure 5 in Goodman et al. (2016)), clearly demonstrate that both the EC2:EC3 and EC1:EC4 interfaces play important roles in determining binding specificity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on observations and mutagenesis experiments and supported by figures and citations.

claim: Pcdh cis multimers have been suggested to form promiscuously between isoforms, and to thereby diversify the functional Pcdh repertoire.
source: Pcdh cis multimers have been suggested to form promiscuously between isoforms, and to thereby diversify the functional Pcdh repertoire (Schreiner and Weiner, 2010; Yagi, 2013; Thu et al., 2014; Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion from previous work and supported by citations.

claim: Domain-deletion studies of numerous Pcdh isoforms localized the cis interaction region to the EC6 domain, with possible contributions from EC5.
source: We previously used domain-deletion studies of numerous Pcdh isoforms to localize the cis interaction region to the EC6 domain, with possible contributions from EC5, and showed that the cis complexes formed are dimeric (Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work and supported by a citation.

claim: The cis complexes formed are dimeric.
source: We previously used domain-deletion studies of numerous Pcdh isoforms to localize the cis interaction region to the EC6 domain, with possible contributions from EC5, and showed that the cis complexes formed are dimeric (Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work and supported by a citation.

claim: Sequence comparisons of Pcdh EC6 domains revealed conserved differences between the Pcdh subfamilies, which are likely to relate to their cis-interaction specificities.
source: Sequence comparisons of Pcdh EC6 domains (Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1) revealed conserved differences between the Pcdh subfamilies, which are likely to relate to their cis-interaction specificities (Thu et al., 2014, Rubinstein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from sequence comparisons and supported by figures and citations.

claim: α-Pcdhs and PcdhγC4 are not transported alone to the cell surface, but only when engaged in cis-dimeric complexes with 'carrier' Pcdhs corresponding to other isoforms.
source: We previously showed subfamily specific diversity in cis interactions in that α-Pcdhs and PcdhγC4 are not transported alone to the cell surface, but only when engaged in cis-dimeric complexes with 'carrier' Pcdhs corresponding to other isoforms, including alternate β and γ, and some C-type Pcdhs (Thu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work and supported by a citation.

claim: Five alternate γB-Pcdhs interacted homophilically in cis in solution, but three alternate γA-Pcdhs did not.
source: Our results suggest additional diversity in Pcdh cis interactions: we found through biophysical measurements that five alternate γB-Pcdhs interacted homophilically in cis in solution (Table 2), but three alternate γA-Pcdhs did not.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from biophysical measurements and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: It is likely that, in general, γA-Pcdhs fail to dimerize or form only weak cis dimers, while alternate γB/γB cis-dimers are expected to have significant affinity.
source: In light of the high level of sequence conservation of the EC6 domains within the γA and within the γB-Pcdh subfamilies (Table 3 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2), it is likely that, in general, γA-Pcdhs fail to dimerize or form only weak cis dimers (enabled in part by the constrained 2D environment of the membrane surface; Wu et al., 2011), while alternate γB/γB cis-dimers are expected to have significant affinity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on sequence conservation and biophysical data and supported by tables, figures, and a citation.

claim: Both the γA- and γB-Pcdhs functioned as carriers for α-Pcdhs.
source: Despite the difference in homodimerization affinities, both the γA- and γB-Pcdhs functioned as carriers for α-Pcdhs (Figure 5A), consistent with the participation of both γA and γB isoforms in Pcdh cis heterodimers.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from cell aggregation assays and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The observations clearly show an unanticipated specificity in cis-dimer formation.
source: Overall, these observations clearly show an unanticipated specificity in cis-dimer formation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: Subfamily specific differences in cis-dimerization specificity are expected to impact the diversity and composition of the functional Pcdh repertoire of cis-dimeric recognition units.
source: Subfamily specific differences in cis-dimerization specificity are expected to impact the diversity and composition of the functional Pcdh repertoire of cis-dimeric recognition units.
evidence: This is stated as an expected consequence of the observed differences.

claim: No recognition units consisting of two alternative α-Pcdh isoforms are expected to form.
source: For example, no recognition units consisting of two alternative α-Pcdh isoforms are expected to form, and γA/γA recognition units would be absent or less frequent than γB/γB recognition units.
evidence: This is stated as an example of the impact of cis-dimerization specificity.

claim: γA/γA recognition units would be absent or less frequent than γB/γB recognition units.
source: For example, no recognition units consisting of two alternative α-Pcdh isoforms are expected to form, and γA/γA recognition units would be absent or less frequent than γB/γB recognition units.
